text.p: Monaco will justifiably be able to celebrate an anticipated transfer of power in French soccer if they beat champions Auxerre in their first division clash in the principality on Sunday.

The leaders, six points ahead of out-of-sorts Paris St Germain and in fine form, are unbeaten at their Louis II stadium this season and have their minds on the job after a successful midweek UEFA Cup trip to Newcastle.

Auxerre, in contrast, have lost all hope of retaining their title -- they are 13 points adrift -- and have their thoughts on revenge against Borussia Dortmund in their European Cup quarter-final second leg on March 19.

The goal from an overhead kick which striker Lilian Laslandes had disallowed, denying Auxerre a first half equaliser in their 3-1 first leg loss at Dortmund on Wednesday, continues to be a bone of contention.
Sabri Lamouchi's second half goal was Auxerre's first in five matches which included French Cup elimination by second division Troyes.
But Laslandes believes Auxerre's improved performance in Dortmund will serve them well in Monaco.

"I think that, this time, the improvment in our game can liberate us. The match at Monaco is going to be very important for us because we need to tell ourselves we really are back on track," Laslandes said.
Auxerre will be without defensive midfielder Christian Henna, who injured a knee during the Dortmund match and is expected to be unavailable for up to six weeks.
Otherwise, they should be able to field the same side that played in Germany.
Monaco should be reinforced by the return from injury of utility defender Emmanuel Petit, who missed the 1-0 UEFA Cup quarter-final first leg win at Newcastle.
Goalkeeper Fabien Barthez has a fractured cheekbone following a clash with Newcastle's Belgian defender Philippe Albert, but is expected to play with a protective mask.
He will probably miss Thursday's match at Rennes after an operation on Monday.

Paris St Germain, their European Cup Winners' Cup title in the balance after failing to break down an ordinary AEK Athens defence on Thursday, turn their attentions to clinging on to second place and a berth in the European Cup Champions' League next season.
They face Lyon at the Parc des Princes where they have not won since mid-November.
